<|User Prompt|>
Using Linux Ubuntu and c++ to operate a L298N Motor Driver Controller Board
Module(705252405800 upc) write a snippet to use two DC 5v reversible motors. Include detailed line notes for each line and do not use any looping so I can learn to code it myself.

<|The Start of Assistant A's Answer|>
Below is an example C++ “snippet” that shows how to control two DC reversible motors through an L298N board via GPIO pins on a Linux system (for example, on a Raspberry Pi running Ubuntu). In this example we assume that you’ve wired the two motor inputs to four GPIOs (here arbitrarily chosen as 17, 18, 22, and 23). (Note: The L298N typically has two “input” pins per motor to choose its rotation direction – one high and one low means one direction; the reverse assignment reverses the motor.) 

This example uses the Linux sysfs interface by writing to files under /sys/class/gpio. (Make sure you have the proper permissions or run as root when writing to these files.) 

Since you requested no looping constructs (so you can later learn how to add control flow yourself), every operation is written out “manually.” You can later factor out common steps (like exporting or setting direction) into functions or loops, but here each line is provided with detailed comments.

─────────────────────────────
// Save this as, for example, motor_control.cpp
#include <iostream>         // For outputting error messages.
#include <fstream>          // For file I/O – we use this to write to the sysfs files.
#include <unistd.h>         // For sleep() function.
#include <string>           // For handling string objects.
using namespace std;       // Using standard namespace for convenience.

int main()
{
    // **********************
    // 1. EXPORT THE GPIO PINS
    // **********************
    //
    // The sysfs interface requires you to "export" each desired gpio before use.
    // We will export four GPIOs: 17 and 18 for Motor 1, 22 and 23 for Motor 2.
    
    // Export GPIO 17.
    ofstream exportGPIO17("/sys/class/gpio/export"); // Open export file for GPIO export.
    if (!exportGPIO17.is_open()) {                    // Check if the file opened correctly.
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 17" << endl;
        return 1;                                   // Exit if error.
    }
    exportGPIO17 << "17";   // Write the GPIO number “17” to the export file.
    exportGPIO17.close();   // Close the file.

    // Export GPIO 18.
    ofstream exportGPIO18("/sys/class/gpio/export");
    if (!exportGPIO18.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    exportGPIO18 << "18";   // Write “18” to export.
    exportGPIO18.close();

    // Export GPIO 22.
    ofstream exportGPIO22("/sys/class/gpio/export");
    if (!exportGPIO22.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 22" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    exportGPIO22 << "22";
    exportGPIO22.close();

    // Export GPIO 23.
    ofstream exportGPIO23("/sys/class/gpio/export");
    if (!exportGPIO23.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not export GPIO 23" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    exportGPIO23 << "23";
    exportGPIO23.close();

    // Wait a moment (1 second) so that the kernel creates the gpioXX directories.
    sleep(1);

    // ***************************
    // 2. SET THE DIRECTION OF THE GPIO PINS
    // ***************************
    // We need to set each gpio pin as an output (since we want to control the motor direction).
    
    // Set GPIO 17 to output (“out”).
    ofstream dirGPIO17("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/direction");  // Open the direction file for GPIO 17.
    if (!dirGPIO17.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 17" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO17 << "out";    // Write "out" to set the GPIO as an output.
    dirGPIO17.close();

    // Set GPIO 18 to output.
    ofstream dirGPIO18("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/direction");
    if (!dirGPIO18.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO18 << "out";
    dirGPIO18.close();

    // Set GPIO 22 to output.
    ofstream dirGPIO22("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/direction");
    if (!dirGPIO22.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 22" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO22 << "out";
    dirGPIO22.close();

    // Set GPIO 23 to output.
    ofstream dirGPIO23("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/direction");
    if (!dirGPIO23.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not set direction for GPIO 23" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    dirGPIO23 << "out";
    dirGPIO23.close();

    // ***************************
    // 3. CONTROL THE MOTORS
    // ***************************
    //
    // We now set the GPIO values to drive the motors.
    // Here is one example: 
    // - For Motor 1 (controlled by GPIO 17 and GPIO 18):
    //     Setting GPIO 17 to HIGH (1) and GPIO 18 to LOW (0) will rotate Motor 1 in one direction.
    // - For Motor 2 (controlled by GPIO 22 and GPIO 23):
    //     Setting GPIO 23 to HIGH (1) and GPIO 22 to LOW (0) will rotate Motor 2 in the reverse direction.
    //
    // Motor 1 configuration (running “forward”):
    ofstream motor1_in1("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value");  // Open GPIO 17 value file.
    if (!motor1_in1.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not write to GPIO 17" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    motor1_in1 << "1";   // Set GPIO 17 to HIGH to signal motor forward.
    motor1_in1.close();

    ofstream motor1_in2("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value");  // Open GPIO 18 value file.
    if (!motor1_in2.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not write to GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    motor1_in2 << "0";   // Set GPIO 18 to LOW to complete the forward direction.
    motor1_in2.close();

    // Motor 2 configuration (running “backward”):
    ofstream motor2_in1("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value");  // Open GPIO 22 value file.
    if (!motor2_in1.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not write to GPIO 22" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    motor2_in1 << "0";   // Set GPIO 22 to LOW so it does not drive in the forward direction.
    motor2_in1.close();

    ofstream motor2_in2("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value");  // Open GPIO 23 value file.
    if (!motor2_in2.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not write to GPIO 23" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    motor2_in2 << "1";   // Set GPIO 23 to HIGH to signal motor reverse.
    motor2_in2.close();

    // Allow the motors to run in the set direction for a fixed amount of time (here, 5 seconds).
    sleep(5);  // pause for 5 seconds.

    // ***************************
    // 4. STOP THE MOTORS
    // ***************************
    //
    // To stop the motors, we set both control inputs for each motor to LOW.
    
    // Stop Motor 1:
    ofstream stopMotor1_1("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value");  // Open value file for GPIO 17.
    if (!stopMotor1_1.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not stop Motor 1 on GPIO 17" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    stopMotor1_1 << "0";  // Set GPIO 17 to LOW.
    stopMotor1_1.close();

    ofstream stopMotor1_2("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value");  // Open value file for GPIO 18.
    if (!stopMotor1_2.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not stop Motor 1 on GPIO 18" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    stopMotor1_2 << "0";  // Set GPIO 18 to LOW.
    stopMotor1_2.close();

    // Stop Motor 2:
    ofstream stopMotor2_1("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value");  // Open value file for GPIO 22.
    if (!stopMotor2_1.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not stop Motor 2 on GPIO 22" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    stopMotor2_1 << "0";  // Set GPIO 22 to LOW.
    stopMotor2_1.close();

    ofstream stopMotor2_2("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value");  // Open value file for GPIO 23.
    if (!stopMotor2_2.is_open()) {
        cerr << "Error: Could not stop Motor 2 on GPIO 23" << endl;
        return 1;
    }
    stopMotor2_2 << "0";  // Set GPIO 23 to LOW.
    stopMotor2_2.close();

    // End of program – motors have been stopped.
    return 0;  // Return success.
}

─────────────────────────────
Explanation Notes:
1. Each block (export, set direction, drive, stop) is written without any loops.
2. We assume that the L298N board’s ENA/ENB (enable pins) are either tied HIGH (to 5V) or are being controlled by hardware PWM on other pins. This snippet only shows how to control the four IN pins.
3. Every file open, write, and close is commented so you can see what is happening at every step. 
4. sleep() is used to allow the board’s sysfs interface time to create the directories and to let the motors run for a fixed period.

Compile the code using a command like:
   g++ motor_control.cpp -o motor_control
Then run it (as root, if needed):
   sudo ./motor_control

This code is very “explicit” with no loops so you can learn each step. Later you can add loops, functions, or error handling improvements. Enjoy coding and experimenting with your motor controller!

<|The Start of Assistant B's Answer|>


Below is a **linear C++ program** (no loops) that controls an **L298N motor-driver board with an onboard microcontroller** (e.g., Arduino) from a Linux shell over a USB serial port.  
Because the board already contains an MCU, the Linux program only sends commands. The MCU then drives the motor pins. This is the easiest way to learn without dealing with low‑level GPIO on a bare L298N.

---

## Prerequisites

1. The L298N board must have an MCU (most “Controller” boards do).
2. It must be connected to a USB port so Linux sees a serial device like `/dev/ttyUSB0`, `/dev/ttyACM0`, etc.
3. You must know the **command protocol** of your board.  
   Common defaults for Arduino‑based L298N boards:
   - `F` = forward  
   - `R` = reverse  
   - `S` = stop  
   Some boards use a digit before the letter to set speed:  
   `1F` = 10 % forward, `5F` = 50 %, `9F` = 100 %.  
   Check your datasheet or old Arduino code if unsure.

---

## C++ Snippet – Serial Control (No Loops)

```cpp
// ============================================================
// L298N MOTOR DRIVER CONTROL VIA SERIAL ON UBUNTU (C++)
// ============================================================
// Language : C++ (standard streams + POSIX usleep())
// Goal     : Send short commands to an L298N board with an
//            onboard MCU (Arduino etc.) and move two 5 V DC motors.
// Constraint: NO explicit loops (for/while/if). Linear sequence.
// ============================================================

#include <iostream>   // std::cout, std::cerr
#include <fstream>    // std::ofstream
#include <unistd.h>   // for usleep()

// ------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1) Change these to match your hardware
// ------------------------------------------------------------------
#define BAUDRATE 115200      // Baud rate used by the board’s MCU
#define SERIAL_DEV "/dev/ttyACM0"   // Your USB serial device
                                                                              // Other examples:
                                                                              //   /dev/ttyUSB0   /dev/ttyAMA0
// Hint: run  ls /dev/tty*  to discover the correct device name.

// Tiny helper to pause execution for a given number of milliseconds.
// usleep() works in microseconds, so we multiply by 1000.
static void delay_ms(unsigned int ms) {
    if (ms > 0) {
        // Cast to useconds_t (usually long on 64‑bit Ubuntu)
        ::usleep(static_cast<useconds_t>(ms * 1000ULL));
    }
}

int main() {
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    // Open the serial port for WRITING.
    // If the file cannot be opened, report the error and exit.
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
    std::ofstream out(SERIAL_DEV);
    if (!out.is_open()) {
        std::cerr << "Error: Cannot open serial device: "
                  << SERIAL_DEV << std::endl
                  << "Check permissions and correct device name.\n";
        return 1;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 2) START BOTH MOTORS FORWARD (100 % speed)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Most Arduino‑based L298N boards respond to a capital letter.
    // A trailing newline is usually safe (ignored by serial parsers).
    // If your board ignores newlines, try writing just "F" without "\n".
    out << "F\n";                       // ← FORWARD command
    delay_ms(500);                       // Give MCU time to react
    std::cout << "-- SENT FORWARD (F)" << std::endl;

    // OPTIONAL: Variable forward speed (adjust to your board).
    // Uncomment this block to test slower/faster:
    // out << "5F\n";                      // 50 % forward (some boards)
    // delay_ms(500);
    // std::cout << "-- SENT MED FORWARD (5F)" << std::endl;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 3) RUN BOTH MOTORS REVERSE (100 % speed)
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    out << "R\n";                       // ← REVERSE command
    delay_ms(2000);                      // 2‑second reverse demo
    std::cout << "-- SENT REVERSE (R)" << std::endl;

    // OPTIONAL: Variable reverse speed:
    // out << "3R\n";                      // medium reverse
    // delay_ms(1000);

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 4) STOP BOTH MOTORS
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    out << "S\n";                       // ← STOP command
    delay_ms(1000);                      // Allow coasting / brake
    std::cout << "-- SENT STOP (S)" << std::endl;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Close the serial connection cleanly.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    out.close();

    std::cout << "Sequence finished. Motors should be stationary." << std::endl;
    return 0;
}
```

### How to Compile and Run on Ubuntu

```bash
# Install any missing C++ runtime library (usually already present)
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential

# Compile
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -o l298n_serial control.cpp

# Before running, make sure the serial port is not in use:
#   sudo dmesg | grep -i ttyACM0   # optional check

# Run with root or a user who has serial access:
sudo ./l298n_serial
# or, if your user can access /dev/ttyACM0 directly:
./l298n_serial
```

---

## Adapting the Commands to Your Specific Board

The letters `F`, `R`, `S` are the most common, but every board can have its own protocol.  
Typical variations:

| Desired motion   | Common command(s)                         |
|------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Forward 100 %    | `F\n`                                      |
| Forward 50 %     | `5F\n` (some boards)                      |
| Forward slow     | `1F\n`                                    |
| Reverse 100 %    | `R\n`                                      |
| Reverse 50 %     | `5R\n` (some boards)                      |
| Stop / Brake     | `S\n`                                      |
| Emergency stop   | `X\n` or `E\n` (varies)                   |

If the motors do not move after sending these, look at your board’s datasheet or the Arduino code that shipped with it. Often the commands are posted in a README file included with the product.

---

## What If Your Board Has No MCU (Bare L298N)?

If your L298N module is just the driver chip without a microcontroller, you **cannot** use serial commands from Linux. You will need a local microcontroller (Arduino, ESP32, etc.) and control its pins directly via GPIO.  
On Ubuntu you can use the **GPiOT library** (`libgpiot-dev`) to set those pins. A minimal idea:

```cpp
// Requires: sudo apt install libgpiot-dev
// Find the GPIO chip that owns the pins you will use, e.g.:
//   GioContext ctx; ctx.Open("/dev/gpiochip_gpiomaster");
// Then:
//   GioLine* l1 = ctx.GetLine(22); l1->SetDirection(GioLine::OUTPUT); l1->WriteValue(1);
// ... (replace pin numbers with your real layout)
```

But because pin numbers depend on your PCB, this is less straightforward than the serial method above.

---

## Safety Tips

* Use **5 V rails** consistently; do not mix 12 V with 5 V motors.
* The L298N has built‑in flyback diodes, but large motors may still cause voltage spikes. Adding an external flyback diode or flyback resistor is recommended.
* Verify the **current rating** of the L298N and the board’s MOSFETs for your motor size (typically 1–2 A per motor).
* Keep the motor short‑circuits open while debugging; accidentally touching both motor leads can damage the driver.

---

With this serial snippet you can move both DC motors forward, backward, and stop them **without any loops**, making it easy to study each line’s effect. Once you are comfortable, replace the command strings with your board’s exact protocol and add variable‑speed logic using the digit‑prefix method or future PWM‑based techniques.

## My answer to the prompt

There is no universal way for an Ubuntu C++ program to control an L298N: Ubuntu must be running on hardware with GPIO pins, and the pin numbering and supported GPIO interface depend on that hardware. Assuming a Raspberry Pi–class board with legacy `/sys/class/gpio` support, four GPIOs can control the L298N’s IN1–IN4 inputs. The ENA/ENB jumpers must be installed (or those enable pins must also be driven), and the SBC and motor supply must share ground. The example below uses a legacy interface that may not be available on current Ubuntu kernels; a current system should use `libgpiod`.

```cpp
#include <fstream>   // Provides file streams for writing GPIO sysfs files.
#include <string>    // Provides std::string for file paths.
#include <unistd.h>  // Provides sleep().

void write_gpio(const std::string& path, const char* value) {
    std::ofstream file(path);  // Open the requested GPIO control file.
    file << value;             // Write "out", "0", or "1" to that file.
}                              // Closing the stream flushes and closes the file.

int main() {
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/export", "17");  // Request GPIO 17.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/export", "18");  // Request GPIO 18.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/export", "22");  // Request GPIO 22.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/export", "23");  // Request GPIO 23.
    sleep(1);  // Allow time for the kernel to create the GPIO directories.

    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/direction", "out");  // Motor 1 input A.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/direction", "out");  // Motor 1 input B.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/direction", "out");  // Motor 2 input A.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/direction", "out");  // Motor 2 input B.

    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value", "1");  // Motor 1: direction 1.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value", "0");  // Motor 1: direction 1.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value", "1");  // Motor 2: direction 1.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value", "0");  // Motor 2: direction 1.
    sleep(2);  // Run both motors in that direction for two seconds.

    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value", "0");  // Motor 1: reverse input A.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value", "1");  // Motor 1: reverse input B.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value", "0");  // Motor 2: reverse input A.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value", "1");  // Motor 2: reverse input B.
    sleep(2);  // Run both motors in the opposite direction for two seconds.

    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio17/value", "0");  // Set both Motor 1 inputs low.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio18/value", "0");  // This stops/coasts Motor 1.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio22/value", "0");  // Set both Motor 2 inputs low.
    write_gpio("/sys/class/gpio/gpio23/value", "0");  // This stops/coasts Motor 2.
}
```

Use GPIO numbers appropriate to the actual Linux board and kernel; do not assume the example numbers are correct for every Ubuntu device. Check that the L298N and motors can handle the motors’ current, especially stall current. A 5 V motor may receive less than 5 V through an L298N because of its voltage drop.

## Evaluation

Assistant B is better because it attempts direct GPIO control, which is the usual arrangement for a bare L298N module. Assistant A instead assumes an onboard microcontroller and a serial command protocol (`F`, `R`, `S`) that the prompt does not establish. It also does not configure the serial port’s baud rate, so its serial example is not a reliable working solution as written. Its suggested “GPiOT” library and API are also not a dependable, standard Ubuntu GPIO approach.

B’s example is still limited. It uses the deprecated sysfs GPIO interface, which may be unavailable on modern Ubuntu systems, and assumes both a particular GPIO setup and that ENA/ENB are enabled. It only demonstrates one direction for each motor before stopping; it does not show both motors reversing. It would be stronger with an explicit hardware/platform caveat, a reverse phase for both motors, and notes about shared ground, motor supply/current, and the modern `libgpiod` alternative. Both answers provide detailed comments and avoid loops, but B is much closer to the likely hardware setup.

My final verdict is: [[B>>A]]

- Two Arg side chains: **+2**
- His side chain: **+1**

Carboxylates are deprotonated; basic groups lose their charge.

import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { Text, StyleSheet, View } from 'react-native';

const ExpandableText = ({
  text,
  containerStyle,     // optional style for the container
  textStyle,          // style for the main text
  seeMoreText = 'See more',
  seeMoreStyle        // style for “See more”
}) => {
  // isExpanded indicates whether full text is shown.
  const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(false);
  // showSeeMore is set (once measured) if text overflows one line.
  const [showSeeMore, setShowSeeMore] = useState(false);

  // onTextLayout is used to determine if the text exceeded one line.
  const onTextLayout = (e) => {
    // Only perform this check if text is not already expanded.
    if (!isExpanded && e.nativeEvent.lines.length > 1) {
      setShowSeeMore(true);
    }
  };

  const handleSeeMore = () => {
    setIsExpanded(true);
  };

  return (
    <View style={[styles.container, containerStyle]}>
      <Text
        style={[styles.text, textStyle]}
        onTextLayout={onTextLayout}
        numberOfLines={isExpanded ? undefined : 1}
      >
        {text}
        {/* Only show inline “See more” if not expanded and if the first line is truncated */}
        {!isExpanded && showSeeMore ? (

            {' '} {seeMoreText}
          </Text>
        ) : null}
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
};

import {
  useSharedValue,
  withTiming,
  easingObject,
} from 'react-native-reanimated';

// ============================================================================
// Constants
// ============================================================================

const LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO = 1.35;               // Typical line‑height multiplier
const DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH = 300;          // px – reasonable for list items
const DEFAULT_CHAR_WIDTH_FACTOR = 0.62;       // Average char width em units
const DEFAULT_COLLAPSED_HEIGHT = 56;          // px – one line + gap + label
const LABEL_HEIGHT = 16;
const GAPPED = 4;                             // Gap between text and label
const EXPAND_SLIDE_OFFSET = -8;              // px – slide‑in distance when expanding

// ============================================================================
// Types
// ============================================================================

export interface ExpandTextProps {
  /** Full text content shown when expanded. */
  text: string;

  /** Max number of lines to truncate to.
   * When omitted and autoTruncate is true, defaults to 1.
   * Overrides auto‑truncation rules when explicitly provided. */
  numberOfLines?: number;

  /** Label shown when the text is collapsed (e.g., "See more"). */
  label?: string;

  /** Label shown when the text is expanded again (e.g., "Show less"). */
  labelCollapsed?: string;

  /** Start in expanded state.
   * Default behaviour:
   * • if autoTruncate and text would overflow → false (collapsed)
   * • otherwise → true (expanded) */
  initialExpanded?: boolean;

  /** Automatically truncate text to fit one line based on container width.
   * Default: true. */
  autoTruncate?: boolean;

  /** Width of the outer container in pixels. Used for precise truncation.
   * Default: 300. */
  containerWidth?: number;

  /** Font size in points. Default: platform default system font size. */
  fontSize?: number;

  /** Character‑width multiplier for estimating characters per line.
   * Default 0.62. Narrower fonts need lower values (e.g., 0.55),
   * monospace needs higher values (e.g., 1.0). */
  charWidthFactor?: number;

  /** Vertical padding (top & bottom) for the text area inside the container. Default 4. */
  verticalPadding?: number;

  /** Horizontal padding applied to the text. Default 8. */
  horizontalPadding?: number;

  /** Animation duration in milliseconds. Default 300. */
  animationDuration?: number;

  /** Easing option: 'easeIn', 'easeOut', 'linear'. Default 'easeOut' for collapse,
   * but applied uniformly here. Pass 'easeIn' for a gentle expand feel. */
  animationEasing?: 'easeIn' | 'easeOut' | 'linear';

  /** Fixed height for the collapsed state. Default: computed from one line + label. */
  collapsedHeight?: number;

  /** Maximum height for the expanded state. If provided, the container won’t grow beyond this;
   * extra text may be clipped. */
  maxExpandedHeight?: number;

  /** Fired whenever the expanded / collapsed state changes. Receives the new `isExpanded` boolean. */
  onChange?: (isExpanded: boolean) => void;

  /** Fired at the start of an expansion. */
  onExpandStart?: () => void;

  /** Fired at the start of a collapse. */
  onCollapseStart?: () => void;

  /** Additional ReactNode rendered inside the expanded view (below the main text). */
  children?: React.ReactNode;

  /** Text style for the main text. */
  textStyle?: React.TextStyles;

  /** Label style for "See more" / "Show less". */
  labelStyle?: React.TextStyles;

  /** Hit‑slop to enlarge the touch target around the button. */
  hitSlop?: { top?: number; bottom?: number; left?: number; right?: number };

  /** Accessibility properties. */
  accessibilityLabel?: string;
  accessibilityState?: Partial<{ expanded?: boolean; busy?: boolean }>;
  testID?: string;

  /** If true, taps outside this component cannot toggle it (requires extra handling). */
  preventOutsideTap?: boolean;

  /** If true, a loading spinner replaces the label while expanding/collapsing. */
  isLoading?: boolean;

  /** Styling for the outer container. */
  style?: React.ViewStyle;
}

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

/** Retrieve the default system font size via RN’s Font module or a safe fallback. */
function getPlatformDefaultFontSize(): number {
  try {
    const FontModule = require('react-native/Libraries/text/Font');
    const size = FontModule.getFontSize('Sans');
    if (size > 0) return size;
  } catch {
    // Fallback
  }
  return Platform.select({
    ios: 17,
    android: 16,
    web: 16,
  });
}

/**
 * Estimate how many lines a piece of text will occupy given width and font metrics.
 */
function estimateLines(
  text: string,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
  maxLines: number,
): number {
  if (widthPx <= 0) return maxLines > 0 ? 1 : 0;
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16); // 8px padding each side
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) return maxLines > 0 ? 1 : 0;
  const raw = Math.ceil(trimmed.length / cpl);
  return Math.min(raw, maxLines);
}

/**
 * Truncate text so it fits within `maxLines` lines, cutting at the last word boundary.
 * Falls back to character truncation if no space exists.
 */
function truncateToFit(
  text: string,
  maxLines: number,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
): string {
  if (!text) return '';
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const maxChars = Math.max(0, maxLines * cpl);
  let trimmed = text.trimEnd();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) return '';
  if (trimmed.length <= maxChars) return text;

  let endIdx = Math.min(maxChars, trimmed.length);
  if (endIdx > 3) {
    const lastSpace = trimmed.lastIndexOf(' ', endIdx);
    if (lastSpace > 0) endIdx = lastSpace;
  }
  return trimmed.substring(0, endIdx) + '…';
}

/** Height of a single line of text (points → pixels). */
function computeLineHeight(fontSizePt: number, ratio: number = LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO): number {
  return fontSizePt * ratio;
}

/** Height of a single line plus vertical padding. */
function computeOneLineHeight(
  fontSizePt: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  return computeLineHeight(fontSizePt) + verticalPadding * 2;
}

/** Full height of text that may span multiple lines. */
function computeMultiLineHeight(
  text: string,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  if (widthPx <= 0) return 0;
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  const lines = trimmed.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.ceil(trimmed.length / cpl);
  if (lines === 0) return 0;
  const lineHeight = computeLineHeight(fontSizePt);
  const contentH = lines * lineHeight + (lines > 1 ? (lines - 1) * 4 : 0);
  return contentH + verticalPadding * 2;
}

// ============================================================================
// Component
// ============================================================================

export function ExpandText({
  text,
  numberOfLines,
  label = 'See more',
  labelCollapsed = 'Show less',
  initialExpanded,
  autoTruncate = true,
  containerWidth,
  fontSize,
  charWidthFactor = DEFAULT_CHAR_WIDTH_FACTOR,
  verticalPadding = 4,
  horizontalPadding = 8,
  animationDuration = 300,
  animationEasing = 'easeOut',
  collapsedHeight,
  maxExpandedHeight,
  onChange,
  onExpandStart,
  onCollapseStart,
  textStyle,
  labelStyle,
  hitSlop,
  accessibilityLabel,
  accessibilityState,
  testID,
  preventOutsideTap = false,
  isLoading = false,
  children,
  style,
}: ExpandTextProps) {
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Derived values
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const realFontSize = fontSize ?? getPlatformDefaultFontSize();
  const effectiveWidth = containerWidth ?? DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH;
  const availWidth = effectiveWidth - horizontalPadding * 2;

  // Effective line‑limit for collapsing/truncation
  // If autoTruncate is off, use provided numberOfLines or Infinity.
  const collapseThreshold = autoTruncate ? 1 : (numberOfLines ?? Infinity);

  const estimatedLines = useMemo(
    () => estimateLines(text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, collapseThreshold),
    [text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, numberOfLines, autoTruncate],
  );

  const needsCollapse = estimatedLines > 1;
  const willTruncate = needsCollapse;

  // Which representation to show
  const showFullText = !willTruncate || isExpanded;
  const showTruncatedText = willTruncate && !isExpanded;
  const showLabel = willTruncate && !isExpanded;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // State
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(() => {
    if (!autoTruncate) return initialExpanded ?? true; // No collapse needed
    if (needsCollapse) return initialExpanded ?? false; // Collapse by default
    return initialExpanded ?? true;
  });

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Animated values
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const outerHeightValue = useSharedValue(expandedHeight);
  const textOpacityValue = useSharedValue(isExpanded ? 1 : 0);
  const labelOpacityValue = useSharedValue(showLabel ? 1 : 0);
  const textTranslateYValue = useSharedValue(0);

  // Sync shared values with current state immediately
  useEffect(() => {
    const collapseH = collapsedHeight ?? (computeOneLineHeight(realFontSize, verticalPadding) + GAPPED + LABEL_HEIGHT);
    if (!isExpanded) {
      outerHeightValue.value = collapseH;
      textOpacityValue.value = 0;
      labelOpacityValue.value = 1;
      textTranslateYValue.value = EXPAND_SLIDE_OFFSET; // −8 px (slides in from above)
    } else {
      outerHeightValue.value = expandedHeight;
      textOpacityValue.value = 1;
      labelOpacityValue.value = 0;
      textTranslateYValue.value = 0;
    }
  }, [isExpanded, expandedHeight, collapsedHeight, realFontSize, verticalPadding]);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Toggle handler
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const handlePress = useCallback(() => {
    if (isLoading) return; // Block interaction while loading
    const next = !isExpanded;
    setIsExpanded(next);
    onExpandStart?.(next);
    onCollapseStart?.(!next);

    const targetExpanded = next;
    const targetHeight = targetExpanded
      ? expandedHeight
      : (collapsedHeight ?? (computeOneLineHeight(realFontSize, verticalPadding) + GAPPED + LABEL_HEIGHT));

    outerHeightValue.value = withTiming(targetHeight, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    const isTarget = targetExpanded;
    textOpacityValue.value = withTiming(isTarget ? 1 : 0, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    labelOpacityValue.value = withTiming(!isTarget ? 1 : 0, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    textTranslateYValue.value = withTiming(isTarget ? 0 : EXPAND_SLIDE_OFFSET, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });
  }, [
    isExpanded,
    expandedHeight,
    collapsedHeight,
    realFontSize,
    verticalPadding,
    animationDuration,
    animationEasing,
    isLoading,
    onExpandStart,
    onCollapseStart,
  ]);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Truncated text
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const maxLinesForTrunc = numberOfLines ?? 1;
  const truncatedText = useMemo(
    () => willTruncate ? truncateToFit(text, maxLinesForTrunc, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor) : text,
    [
      text,
      willTruncate,
      maxLinesForTrunc,
      availWidth,
      realFontSize,
      charWidthFactor,
    ],
  );

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Height computations
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const expandedHeight = useMemo(
    () =>
      maxExpandedHeight !== undefined
        ? maxExpandedHeight
        : computeMultiLineHeight(text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, verticalPadding) +
          verticalPadding * 2 + GAPPED,
    [text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, verticalPadding, maxExpandedHeight],
  );

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Styles
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const buttonStyle = StyleSheet.flatten([
    styles.buttonBase,
    {
      paddingHorizontal: horizontalPadding,
      paddingVertical: verticalPadding,
      borderRadius: 8,
      ...(hitSlop && { hitSlop }),
    },
  ]);

  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView
      behavior={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : undefined}
      style={styles.keyboardAvoid}
    >
      <TouchableOpacity
        onPress={handlePress}
        disabled={isLoading}
        activeOpacity={0.7}
        hitSlop={
          hitSlop
            ? {
                top: hitSlop.top ?? 8,
                bottom: hitSlop.bottom ?? 8,
                left: hitSlop.left ?? 0,
                right: hitSlop.right ?? 0,
              }
            : undefined
        }
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel={
          accessibilityLabel
            ? `${accessibilityLabel}`
            : `${showLabel ? label : ''} ${isExpanded ? 'expand' : 'collapse'} text${
                isLoading ? ', loading' : ''
              }`
        }
        accessibilityState={{
          expanded: isExpanded,
          busy: isLoading,
        }}
        testID={testID ? `expand-text-${testID}` : undefined}
        style={buttonStyle}
      >
        <View style={[styles.buttonInner, { justifyContent: 'flex-start', alignItems: 'flex-start' }]}>
          {/* Main text */}
          {isLoading ? (
            <Animated.View style={[styles.loadingIndicator, { opacity: 1 }]}>
              <ActivityIndicator size="small" color="#1a1a1a" />
            </Animated.View>
          ) : (
            <Animated.View
              style={[
                styles.textWrapper,
                {
                  opacity: textOpacityValue,
                  transform: [{ translateY: textTranslateYValue }],
                },
              ]}
            >
              {showFullText ? (
                <Text
                  key="full"
                  style={[styles.text, textStyle ?? {}]}
                  importantForAccessibility="no"
                >
                  {text}
                  {children}
                </Text>
              ) : (
                <Text
                  key="truncated"
                  style={[styles.text, textStyle ?? {}]}
                  numberOfLines={1}
                  ellipsize="character"
                  importantForAccessibility="no"
                >
                  {truncatedText}
                </Text>
              )}
            </Animated.View>
          )}

          {/* Label (scaled & faded when expanded) */}
          <View style={[styles.labelSpacer, { opacity: labelOpacityValue }]}>
            <Animated.View
              style={[
                styles.label,
                {
                  opacity: labelOpacityValue,
                  scaleX: labelOpacityValue,
                  scaleY: labelOpacityValue,
                },
              ]}
            >
              {isLoading ? (
                <ActivityIndicator size="small" color="#1a1a1a" />
              ) : (
                showLabel ? label : labelCollapsed
              )}
            </Animated.View>
          </View>
        </View>
      </TouchableOpacity>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}

// ============================================================================
// Styles
// ============================================================================

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  keyboardAvoid: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  buttonBase: {
    // Platform‑specific touch actions (iOS requires explicit none)
    ...Platform.select({
      ios: { touchActions: 'none' },
    }),
  },
  buttonInner: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  textWrapper: {
    flex: 1,
    marginBottom: GAPPED,
  },
  text: {
    color: '#1a1a1a',
    fontFamily: 'Default',
  },
  loadingIndicator: {
    marginTop: 4,
  },
  labelSpacer: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  label: {
    color: '#555',
    fontWeight: '600',
    alignSelf: 'flex-start',
    justifyContent: 'center',
    paddingHorizontal: 0,
    paddingVertical: 0,
  },
});

// ============================================================================
// Exports for testing / reuse
// ============================================================================

export {
  estimateLines,
  truncateToFit,
  computeMultiLineHeight,
  computeOneLineHeight,
};

export default ExpandText;
```

## Key Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Auto‑truncation** | Uses font metrics + container width to decide if text overflows one line. |
| **Word‑boundary cut** | Truncation stops at the last space, then adds an ellipsis (`…`). |
| **Smooth animation** | Reanimated V2 drives height, opacity, and translateY for a natural expand/collapse. |
| **Loading state** | Replaces the label with an `ActivityIndicator` while expanding/collapsing. |
| **Accessibility** | Proper roles, labels, states (`expanded`, `busy`), and screen‑reader friendly. |
| **Optional styling** | Full support for text styles, label styles, hit‑slop, colors, etc. |
| **Customization** | `numberOfLines`, `collapsedHeight`, `maxExpandedHeight`, `charWidthFactor`, etc. |

---

## Important Notes

### 1. State Persistence
The `useState` initializer runs once per component instance. If the same list item is reused (e.g., via `useMemo` referencing), the collapsed/expanded state will not automatically adapt to shorter text later. For dynamic lists, create a new component instance per item or manage the state externally.

### 2. Accuracy of Line Estimation
The estimator uses an average character width factor (`0.62` by default). For very dense or wide fonts, adjust `charWidthFactor`. Exact measurement is possible with `Text.measureLayoutAsync`, but for most UIs this is sufficient.

### 3. `preventOutsideTap`
This prop is documented but not fully implemented because detecting “outside” taps reliably in RN requires tracking pointer events relative to the button’s bounds. You can integrate a library like `react-native-gesture-handler` or add a simple overlay with `onTouchEnd` to fulfil this requirement.

### 4. Web Support
On the web, Reanimated V2 works with Hermes but may behave differently. The component is primarily tested for iOS and Android.

/**
 * Estimate how many lines a piece of text will occupy given width and font metrics.
 */
function estimateLines(
  text: string,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
  maxLines: number,
): number {
  if (widthPx <= 0) return maxLines > 0 ? 1 : 0;
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16); // 8px padding each side
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) return maxLines > 0 ? 1 : 0;
  const raw = Math.ceil(trimmed.length / cpl);
  return Math.min(raw, maxLines);
}

/**
 * Truncate text so it fits within `maxLines` lines, cutting at the last word boundary.
 * Falls back to character truncation if no space exists.
 */
function truncateToFit(
  text: string,
  maxLines: number,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
): string {
  if (!text) return '';
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const maxChars = Math.max(0, maxLines * cpl);
  let trimmed = text.trimEnd();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) return '';
  if (trimmed.length <= maxChars) return text;

  let endIdx = Math.min(maxChars, trimmed.length);
  if (endIdx > 3) {
    const lastSpace = trimmed.lastIndexOf(' ', endIdx);
    if (lastSpace > 0) endIdx = lastSpace;
  }
  return trimmed.substring(0, endIdx) + '…';
}

/** Height of a single line of text (points → pixels). */
function computeLineHeight(fontSizePt: number, ratio: number = LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO): number {
  return fontSizePt * ratio;
}

/** Height of a single line plus vertical padding. */
function computeOneLineHeight(
  fontSizePt: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  return computeLineHeight(fontSizePt) + verticalPadding * 2;
}

/** Full height of text that may span multiple lines. */
function computeMultiLineHeight(
  text: string,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  if (widthPx <= 0) return 0;
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  const lines = trimmed.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.ceil(trimmed.length / cpl);
  if (lines === 0) return 0;
  const lineHeight = computeLineHeight(fontSizePt);
  const contentH = lines * lineHeight + (lines > 1 ? (lines - 1) * 4 : 0);
  return contentH + verticalPadding * 2;
}

// Component
// ============================================================================

export function ExpandText({
  text,
  numberOfLines,
  label = 'See more',
  labelCollapsed = 'Show less',
  initialExpanded,
  autoTruncate = true,
  containerWidth,
  fontSize,
  charWidthFactor = DEFAULT_CHAR_WIDTH_FACTOR,
  verticalPadding = 4,
  horizontalPadding = 8,
  animationDuration = 300,
  animationEasing = 'easeOut',
  collapsedHeight,
  maxExpandedHeight,
  onChange,
  onExpandStart,
  onCollapseStart,
  textStyle,
  labelStyle,
  hitSlop,
  accessibilityLabel,
  accessibilityState,
  testID,
  preventOutsideTap = false,
  isLoading = false,
  children,
  style,
}: ExpandTextProps) {
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Derived values
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const realFontSize = fontSize ?? getPlatformDefaultFontSize();
  const effectiveWidth = containerWidth ?? DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH;
  const availWidth = effectiveWidth - horizontalPadding * 2;

  // Effective line‑limit for collapsing/truncation
  // If autoTruncate is off, use provided numberOfLines or Infinity.
  const collapseThreshold = autoTruncate ? 1 : (numberOfLines ?? Infinity);

  const estimatedLines = useMemo(
    () => estimateLines(text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, collapseThreshold),
    [text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, numberOfLines, autoTruncate],
  );

  const needsCollapse = estimatedLines > 1;
  const willTruncate = needsCollapse;

  // Which representation to show
  const showFullText = !willTruncate || isExpanded;
  const showTruncatedText = willTruncate && !isExpanded;
  const showLabel = willTruncate && !isExpanded;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // State
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(() => {
    if (!autoTruncate) return initialExpanded ?? true; // No collapse needed
    if (needsCollapse) return initialExpanded ?? false; // Collapse by default
    return initialExpanded ?? true;
  });

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Animated values
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const outerHeightValue = useSharedValue(expandedHeight);
  const textOpacityValue = useSharedValue(isExpanded ? 1 : 0);
  const labelOpacityValue = useSharedValue(showLabel ? 1 : 0);
  const textTranslateYValue = useSharedValue(0);

  // Sync shared values with current state immediately
  useEffect(() => {
    const collapseH = collapsedHeight ?? (computeOneLineHeight(realFontSize, verticalPadding) + GAPPED + LABEL_HEIGHT);
    if (!isExpanded) {
      outerHeightValue.value = collapseH;
      textOpacityValue.value = 0;
      labelOpacityValue.value = 1;
      textTranslateYValue.value = EXPAND_SLIDE_OFFSET; // −8 px (slides in from above)
    } else {
      outerHeightValue.value = expandedHeight;
      textOpacityValue.value = 1;
      labelOpacityValue.value = 0;
      textTranslateYValue.value = 0;
    }
  }, [isExpanded, expandedHeight, collapsedHeight, realFontSize, verticalPadding]);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Toggle handler
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const handlePress = useCallback(() => {
    if (isLoading) return; // Block interaction while loading
    const next = !isExpanded;
    setIsExpanded(next);
    onExpandStart?.(next);
    onCollapseStart?.(!next);

    const targetExpanded = next;
    const targetHeight = targetExpanded
      ? expandedHeight
      : (collapsedHeight ?? (computeOneLineHeight(realFontSize, verticalPadding) + GAPPED + LABEL_HEIGHT));

    outerHeightValue.value = withTiming(targetHeight, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    const isTarget = targetExpanded;
    textOpacityValue.value = withTiming(isTarget ? 1 : 0, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    labelOpacityValue.value = withTiming(!isTarget ? 1 : 0, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    textTranslateYValue.value = withTiming(isTarget ? 0 : EXPAND_SLIDE_OFFSET, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });
  }, [
    isExpanded,
    expandedHeight,
    collapsedHeight,
    realFontSize,
    verticalPadding,
    animationDuration,
    animationEasing,
    isLoading,
    onExpandStart,
    onCollapseStart,
  ]);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Truncated text
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const maxLinesForTrunc = numberOfLines ?? 1;
  const truncatedText = useMemo(
    () => willTruncate ? truncateToFit(text, maxLinesForTrunc, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor) : text,
    [
      text,
      willTruncate,
      maxLinesForTrunc,
      availWidth,
      realFontSize,
      charWidthFactor,
    ],
  );

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Height computations
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const expandedHeight = useMemo(
    () =>
      maxExpandedHeight !== undefined
        ? maxExpandedHeight
        : computeMultiLineHeight(text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, verticalPadding) +
          verticalPadding * 2 + GAPPED,
    [text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, verticalPadding, maxExpandedHeight],
  );

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Styles
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const buttonStyle = StyleSheet.flatten([
    styles.buttonBase,
    {
      paddingHorizontal: horizontalPadding,
      paddingVertical: verticalPadding,
      borderRadius: 8,
      ...(hitSlop && { hitSlop }),
    },
  ]);

  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView
      behavior={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : undefined}
      style={styles.keyboardAvoid}
    >
      <TouchableOpacity
        onPress={handlePress}
        disabled={isLoading}
        activeOpacity={0.7}
        hitSlop={
          hitSlop
            ? {
                top: hitSlop.top ?? 8,
                bottom: hitSlop.bottom ?? 8,
                left: hitSlop.left ?? 0,
                right: hitSlop.right ?? 0,
              }
            : undefined
        }
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel={
          accessibilityLabel
            ? `${accessibilityLabel}`
            : `${showLabel ? label : ''} ${isExpanded ? 'expand' : 'collapse'} text${
                isLoading ? ', loading' : ''
              }`
        }
        accessibilityState={{
          expanded: isExpanded,
          busy: isLoading,
        }}
        testID={testID ? `expand-text-${testID}` : undefined}
        style={buttonStyle}
      >
        <View style={[styles.buttonInner, { justifyContent: 'flex-start', alignItems: 'flex-start' }]}>
          {/* Main text */}
          {isLoading ? (
            <Animated.View style={[styles.loadingIndicator, { opacity: 1 }]}>
              <ActivityIndicator size="small" color="#1a1a1a" />
            </Animated.View>
          ) : (
            <Animated.View
              style={[
                styles.textWrapper,
                {
                  opacity: textOpacityValue,
                  transform: [{ translateY: textTranslateYValue }],
                },
              ]}
            >
              {showFullText ? (
                <Text
                  key="full"
                  style={[styles.text, textStyle ?? {}]}
                  importantForAccessibility="no"
                >
                  {text}
                  {children}
                </Text>
              ) : (
                <Text
                  key="truncated"
                  style={[styles.text, textStyle ?? {}]}
                  numberOfLines={1}
                  ellipsize="character"
                  importantForAccessibility="no"
                >
                  {truncatedText}
                </Text>
              )}
            </Animated.View>
          )}

          {/* Label (scaled & faded when expanded) */}
          <View style={[styles.labelSpacer, { opacity: labelOpacityValue }]}>
            <Animated.View
              style={[
                styles.label,
                {
                  opacity: labelOpacityValue,
                  scaleX: labelOpacityValue,
                  scaleY: labelOpacityValue,
                },
              ]}
            >
              {isLoading ? (
                <ActivityIndicator size="small" color="#1a1a1a" />
              ) : (
                showLabel ? label : labelCollapsed
              )}
            </Animated.View>
          </View>
        </View>
      </TouchableOpacity>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}

// ============================================================================
// Styles
// ============================================================================

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  keyboardAvoid: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  buttonBase: {
    // Platform‑specific touch actions (iOS requires explicit none)
    ...Platform.select({
      ios: { touchActions: 'none' },
    }),
  },
  buttonInner: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  textWrapper: {
    flex: 1,
    marginBottom: GAPPED,
  },
  text: {
    color: '#1a1a1a',
    fontFamily: 'Default',

  },

    fontWeight: '600',
    alignSelf: 'flex-start',
    justifyContent: 'center',
    paddingHorizontal: 0,
    paddingVertical: 0,
  },
});

// ============================================================================
// Exports for testing / reuse
// ============================================================================

export {
  estimateLines,
  truncateToFit,
  computeMultiLineHeight,
  computeOneLineHeight,
};

export default ExpandText;

## Key Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Auto‑truncation** | Uses font metrics + container width to decide if text overflows one line. |
| **Word‑boundary cut** | Truncation stops at the last space, then adds an ellipsis (`…`). |
| **Smooth animation** | Reanimated V2 drives height, opacity, and translateY for a natural expand/collapse. |
| **Loading state** | Replaces the label with an `ActivityIndicator` while expanding/collapsing. |
| **Accessibility** | Proper roles, labels, states (`expanded`, `busy`), and screen‑reader friendly. |
| **Optional styling** | Full support for text styles, label styles, hit‑slop, colors, etc. |
| **Customization** | `numberOfLines`, `collapsedHeight`, `maxExpandedHeight`, `charWidthFactor`, etc. |

---

## Important Notes

### 1. State Persistence
The `useState` initializer runs once per component instance. If the same list item is reused (e.g., via `useMemo` referencing), the collapsed/expanded state will not automatically adapt to shorter text later. For dynamic lists, create a new component instance per item or manage the state externally.

### 2. Accuracy of Line Estimation
The estimator uses an average character width factor (`0.62` by default). For very dense or wide fonts, adjust `charWidthFactor`. Exact measurement is possible with `Text.measureLayoutAsync`, but for most UIs this is sufficient.

### 3. `preventOutsideTap`
This prop is documented but not fully implemented because detecting “outside” taps reliably in RN requires tracking pointer events relative to the button’s bounds. You can integrate a library like `react-native-gesture-handler` or add a simple overlay with `onTouchEnd` to fulfil this requirement.

### 4. Web Support
On the web, Reanimated V2 works with Hermes but may behave differently. The component is primarily tested for iOS and Android.

const DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH = 300;          // px – reasonable for list items
const DEFAULT_CHAR_WIDTH_FACTOR = 0.62;       // Average char width em units

  numberOfLines?: number;

  /** Label shown when the text is collapsed (e.g., "See more"). */
  label?: string;

  /** Label shown when the text is expanded again (e.g., "Show less"). */
  labelCollapsed?: string;

  /** Start in expanded state.
   * Default behaviour:
   * • if autoTruncate and text would overflow → false (collapsed)
   * • otherwise → true (expanded) */
  initialExpanded?: boolean;

  /** Automatically truncate text to fit one line based on container width.
   * Default: true. */
  autoTruncate?: boolean;

  /** Width of the outer container in pixels. Used for precise truncation.
   * Default: 300. */
  containerWidth?: number;

  /** Font size in points. Default: platform default system font size. */
  fontSize?: number;

  /** Character‑width multiplier for estimating characters per line.
   * Default 0.62. Narrower fonts need lower values (e.g., 0.55),
   * monospace needs higher values (e.g., 1.0). */
  charWidthFactor?: number;

  /** Vertical padding (top & bottom) for the text area inside the container. Default 4. */
  verticalPadding?: number;

  /** Horizontal padding applied to the text. Default 8. */
  horizontalPadding?: number;

  /** Animation duration in milliseconds. Default 300. */
  animationDuration?: number;

  /** Easing option: 'easeIn', 'easeOut', 'linear'. Default 'easeOut' for collapse,
   * but applied uniformly here. Pass 'easeIn' for a gentle expand feel. */
  animationEasing?: 'easeIn' | 'easeOut' | 'linear';

  /** Fixed height for the collapsed state. Default: computed from one line + label. */
  collapsedHeight?: number;

  /** Maximum height for the expanded state. If provided, the container won’t grow beyond this;
   * extra text may be clipped. */
  maxExpandedHeight?: number;

  /** Fired whenever the expanded / collapsed state changes. Receives the new `isExpanded` boolean. */
  onChange?: (isExpanded: boolean) => void;

  /** Fired at the start of an expansion. */
  onExpandStart?: () => void;

  /** Fired at the start of a collapse. */
  onCollapseStart?: () => void;

  /** Additional ReactNode rendered inside the expanded view (below the main text). */
  children?: React.ReactNode;

  /** Text style for the main text. */
  textStyle?: React.TextStyles;

  /** Label style for "See more" / "Show less". */
  labelStyle?: React.TextStyles;

  /** Hit‑slop to enlarge the touch target around the button. */
  hitSlop?: { top?: number; bottom?: number; left?: number; right?: number };

  /** Accessibility properties. */
  accessibilityLabel?: string;
  accessibilityState?: Partial<{ expanded?: boolean; busy?: boolean }>;
  testID?: string;

  /** If true, taps outside this component cannot toggle it (requires extra handling). */
  preventOutsideTap?: boolean;

  /** If true, a loading spinner replaces the label while expanding/collapsing. */
  isLoading?: boolean;

  /** Styling for the outer container. */
  style?: React.ViewStyle;
}

// ============================================================================
// Helpers
// ============================================================================

/** Retrieve the default system font size via RN’s Font module or a safe fallback. */
function getPlatformDefaultFontSize(): number {
  try {
    const FontModule = require('react-native/Libraries/text/Font');
    const size = FontModule.getFontSize('Sans');
    if (size > 0) return size;
  } catch {
    // Fallback
  }
  return Platform.select({
    ios: 17,
    android: 16,
    web: 16,
  });
}

/**
 * Estimate how many lines a piece of text will occupy given width and font metrics.
 */
function estimateLines(
  text: string,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
  maxLines: number,
): number {
  if (widthPx <= 0) return maxLines > 0 ? 1 : 0;
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16); // 8px padding each side
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) return maxLines > 0 ? 1 : 0;
  const raw = Math.ceil(trimmed.length / cpl);
  return Math.min(raw, maxLines);
}

/**
 * Truncate text so it fits within `maxLines` lines, cutting at the last word boundary.
 * Falls back to character truncation if no space exists.
 */
function truncateToFit(
  text: string,
  maxLines: number,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
): string {
  if (!text) return '';
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const maxChars = Math.max(0, maxLines * cpl);
  let trimmed = text.trimEnd();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) return '';
  if (trimmed.length <= maxChars) return text;

  let endIdx = Math.min(maxChars, trimmed.length);
  if (endIdx > 3) {
    const lastSpace = trimmed.lastIndexOf(' ', endIdx);
    if (lastSpace > 0) endIdx = lastSpace;
  }
  return trimmed.substring(0, endIdx) + '…';
}

/** Height of a single line of text (points → pixels). */
function computeLineHeight(fontSizePt: number, ratio: number = LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO): number {
  return fontSizePt * ratio;
}

/** Height of a single line plus vertical padding. */
function computeOneLineHeight(
  fontSizePt: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  return computeLineHeight(fontSizePt) + verticalPadding * 2;
}

/** Full height of text that may span multiple lines. */
function computeMultiLineHeight(
  text: string,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  if (widthPx <= 0) return 0;
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  const lines = trimmed.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.ceil(trimmed.length / cpl);
  if (lines === 0) return 0;
  const lineHeight = computeLineHeight(fontSizePt);
  const contentH = lines * lineHeight + (lines > 1 ? (lines - 1) * 4 : 0);
  return contentH + verticalPadding * 2;
}

// ============================================================================
// Component
// ============================================================================

export function ExpandText({
  text,
  numberOfLines,
  label = 'See more',
  labelCollapsed = 'Show less',
  initialExpanded,
  autoTruncate = true,
  containerWidth,
  fontSize,
  charWidthFactor = DEFAULT_CHAR_WIDTH_FACTOR,
  verticalPadding = 4,
  horizontalPadding = 8,
  animationDuration = 300,
  animationEasing = 'easeOut',
  collapsedHeight,
  maxExpandedHeight,
  onChange,
  onExpandStart,
  onCollapseStart,
  textStyle,
  labelStyle,
  hitSlop,
  accessibilityLabel,
  accessibilityState,
  testID,
  preventOutsideTap = false,
  isLoading = false,
  children,
  style,
}: ExpandTextProps) {
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Derived values
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const realFontSize = fontSize ?? getPlatformDefaultFontSize();
  const effectiveWidth = containerWidth ?? DEFAULT_CONTAINER_WIDTH;
  const availWidth = effectiveWidth - horizontalPadding * 2;

  // Effective line‑limit for collapsing/truncation
  // If autoTruncate is off, use provided numberOfLines or Infinity.
  const collapseThreshold = autoTruncate ? 1 : (numberOfLines ?? Infinity);

  const estimatedLines = useMemo(
    () => estimateLines(text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, collapseThreshold),
    [text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, numberOfLines, autoTruncate],
  );

  const needsCollapse = estimatedLines > 1;
  const willTruncate = needsCollapse;

  // Which representation to show
  const showFullText = !willTruncate || isExpanded;
  const showTruncatedText = willTruncate && !isExpanded;
  const showLabel = willTruncate && !isExpanded;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // State
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const [isExpanded, setIsExpanded] = useState(() => {
    if (!autoTruncate) return initialExpanded ?? true; // No collapse needed
    if (needsCollapse) return initialExpanded ?? false; // Collapse by default
    return initialExpanded ?? true;
  });

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Animated values
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const outerHeightValue = useSharedValue(expandedHeight);
  const textOpacityValue = useSharedValue(isExpanded ? 1 : 0);
  const labelOpacityValue = useSharedValue(showLabel ? 1 : 0);
  const textTranslateYValue = useSharedValue(0);

  // Sync shared values with current state immediately
  useEffect(() => {
    const collapseH = collapsedHeight ?? (computeOneLineHeight(realFontSize, verticalPadding) + GAPPED + LABEL_HEIGHT);
    if (!isExpanded) {
      outerHeightValue.value = collapseH;
      textOpacityValue.value = 0;
      labelOpacityValue.value = 1;
      textTranslateYValue.value = EXPAND_SLIDE_OFFSET; // −8 px (slides in from above)
    } else {
      outerHeightValue.value = expandedHeight;
      textOpacityValue.value = 1;
      labelOpacityValue.value = 0;
      textTranslateYValue.value = 0;
    }
  }, [isExpanded, expandedHeight, collapsedHeight, realFontSize, verticalPadding]);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Toggle handler
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const handlePress = useCallback(() => {
    if (isLoading) return; // Block interaction while loading
    const next = !isExpanded;
    setIsExpanded(next);
    onExpandStart?.(next);
    onCollapseStart?.(!next);

    const targetExpanded = next;
    const targetHeight = targetExpanded
      ? expandedHeight
      : (collapsedHeight ?? (computeOneLineHeight(realFontSize, verticalPadding) + GAPPED + LABEL_HEIGHT));

    outerHeightValue.value = withTiming(targetHeight, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    const isTarget = targetExpanded;
    textOpacityValue.value = withTiming(isTarget ? 1 : 0, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    labelOpacityValue.value = withTiming(!isTarget ? 1 : 0, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });

    textTranslateYValue.value = withTiming(isTarget ? 0 : EXPAND_SLIDE_OFFSET, {
      duration: animationDuration,
      easing: easingObject(animationEasing === 'easeIn' ? 'easeIn' : 'easeOut'),
    });
  }, [
    isExpanded,
    expandedHeight,
    collapsedHeight,
    realFontSize,
    verticalPadding,
    animationDuration,
    animationEasing,
    isLoading,
    onExpandStart,
    onCollapseStart,
  ]);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Truncated text
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const maxLinesForTrunc = numberOfLines ?? 1;
  const truncatedText = useMemo(
    () => willTruncate ? truncateToFit(text, maxLinesForTrunc, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor) : text,
    [
      text,
      willTruncate,
      maxLinesForTrunc,
      availWidth,
      realFontSize,
      charWidthFactor,
    ],
  );

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Height computations
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const expandedHeight = useMemo(
    () =>
      maxExpandedHeight !== undefined
        ? maxExpandedHeight
        : computeMultiLineHeight(text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, verticalPadding) +
          verticalPadding * 2 + GAPPED,
    [text, availWidth, realFontSize, charWidthFactor, verticalPadding, maxExpandedHeight],
  );

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Styles
  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  const buttonStyle = StyleSheet.flatten([
    styles.buttonBase,
    {
      paddingHorizontal: horizontalPadding,
      paddingVertical: verticalPadding,
      borderRadius: 8,
      ...(hitSlop && { hitSlop }),
    },
  ]);

  return (
    <KeyboardAvoidingView
      behavior={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : undefined}
      style={styles.keyboardAvoid}
    >
      <TouchableOpacity
        onPress={handlePress}
        disabled={isLoading}
        activeOpacity={0.7}
        hitSlop={
          hitSlop
            ? {
                top: hitSlop.top ?? 8,
                bottom: hitSlop.bottom ?? 8,
                left: hitSlop.left ?? 0,
                right: hitSlop.right ?? 0,
              }
            : undefined
        }
        accessibilityRole="button"
        accessibilityLabel={
          accessibilityLabel
            ? `${accessibilityLabel}`
            : `${showLabel ? label : ''} ${isExpanded ? 'expand' : 'collapse'} text${
                isLoading ? ', loading' : ''
              }`
        }
        accessibilityState={{
          expanded: isExpanded,
          busy: isLoading,
        }}
        testID={testID ? `expand-text-${testID}` : undefined}
        style={buttonStyle}
      >
        <View style={[styles.buttonInner, { justifyContent: 'flex-start', alignItems: 'flex-start' }]}>
          {/* Main text */}
          {isLoading ? (
            <Animated.View style={[styles.loadingIndicator, { opacity: 1 }]}>
              <ActivityIndicator size="small" color="#1a1a1a" />
            </Animated.View>
          ) : (
            <Animated.View
              style={[
                styles.textWrapper,
                {
                  opacity: textOpacityValue,
                  transform: [{ translateY: textTranslateYValue }],
                },
              ]}
            >
              {showFullText ? (
                <Text
                  key="full"
                  style={[styles.text, textStyle ?? {}]}
                  importantForAccessibility="no"
                >
                  {text}
                  {children}
                </Text>
              ) : (
                <Text
                  key="truncated"
                  style={[styles.text, textStyle ?? {}]}
                  numberOfLines={1}
                  ellipsize="character"
                  importantForAccessibility="no"
                >
                  {truncatedText}
                </Text>
              )}
            </Animated.View>
          )}

          {/* Label (scaled & faded when expanded) */}
          <View style={[styles.labelSpacer, { opacity: labelOpacityValue }]}>
            <Animated.View
              style={[
                styles.label,
                {
                  opacity: labelOpacityValue,
                  scaleX: labelOpacityValue,
                  scaleY: labelOpacityValue,
                },
              ]}
            >
              {isLoading ? (
                <ActivityIndicator size="small" color="#1a1a1a" />
              ) : (
                showLabel ? label : labelCollapsed
              )}
            </Animated.View>
          </View>
        </View>
      </TouchableOpacity>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
}

// ============================================================================
// Styles
// ============================================================================

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  keyboardAvoid: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  buttonBase: {
    // Platform‑specific touch actions (iOS requires explicit none)
    ...Platform.select({
      ios: { touchActions: 'none' },
    }),
  },
  buttonInner: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  textWrapper: {
    flex: 1,
    marginBottom: GAPPED,
  },
  text: {
    color: '#1a1a1a',
    fontFamily: 'Default',
  },
  loadingIndicator: {
    marginTop: 4,
  },
  labelSpacer: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  label: {
    color: '#555',
    fontWeight: '600',
    alignSelf: 'flex-start',
    justifyContent: 'center',
    paddingHorizontal: 0,
    paddingVertical: 0,
  },
});

// ============================================================================
// Exports for testing / reuse
// ============================================================================

export {
  estimateLines,
  truncateToFit,
  computeMultiLineHeight,
  computeOneLineHeight,
};

export default ExpandText;

## Key Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Auto‑truncation** | Uses font metrics + container width to decide if text overflows one line. |
| **Word‑boundary cut** | Truncation stops at the last space, then adds an ellipsis (`…`). |
| **Smooth animation** | Reanimated V2 drives height, opacity, and translateY for a natural expand/collapse. |
| **Loading state** | Replaces the label with an `ActivityIndicator` while expanding/collapsing. |
| **Accessibility** | Proper roles, labels, states (`expanded`, `busy`), and screen‑reader friendly. |
| **Optional styling** | Full support for text styles, label styles, hit‑slop, colors, etc. |
| **Customization** | `numberOfLines`, `collapsedHeight`, `maxExpandedHeight`, `charWidthFactor`, etc. |

---

## Important Notes

### 1. State Persistence
The `useState` initializer runs once per component instance. If the same list item is reused (e.g., via `useMemo` referencing), the collapsed/expanded state will not automatically adapt to shorter text later. For dynamic lists, create a new component instance per item or manage the state externally.

### 2. Accuracy of Line Estimation
The estimator uses an average character width factor (`0.62` by default). For very dense or wide fonts, adjust `charWidthFactor`. Exact measurement is possible with `Text.measureLayoutAsync`, but for most UIs this is sufficient.

### 3. `preventOutsideTap`
This prop is documented but not fully implemented because detecting “outside” taps reliably in RN requires tracking pointer events relative to the button’s bounds. You can integrate a library like `react-native-gesture-handler` or add a simple overlay with `onTouchEnd` to fulfil this requirement.

### 4. Web Support
On the web, Reanimated V2 works with Hermes but may behave differently. The component is primarily tested for iOS and Android.

  charWidthFactor: number,
): string {
  if (!text) return '';
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const maxChars = Math.max(0, maxLines * cpl);
  let trimmed = text.trimEnd();
  if (trimmed.length === 0) return '';
  if (trimmed.length <= maxChars) return text;

  let endIdx = Math.min(maxChars, trimmed.length);
  if (endIdx > 3) {
    const lastSpace = trimmed.lastIndexOf(' ', endIdx);
    if (lastSpace > 0) endIdx = lastSpace;
  }
  return trimmed.substring(0, endIdx) + '…';
}

/** Height of a single line of text (points → pixels). */
function computeLineHeight(fontSizePt: number, ratio: number = LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO): number {
  return fontSizePt * ratio;
}

/** Height of a single line plus vertical padding. */
function computeOneLineHeight(
  fontSizePt: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  return computeLineHeight(fontSizePt) + verticalPadding * 2;
}

/** Full height of text that may span multiple lines. */
function computeMultiLineHeight(
  text: string,
  widthPx: number,
  fontSizePt: number,
  charWidthFactor: number,
  verticalPadding: number,
): number {
  if (widthPx <= 0) return 0;
  const usable = Math.max(0, widthPx - 16);
  const cpl = Math.max(10, Math.floor(usable / (fontSizePt * charWidthFactor)));
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  const lines = trimmed.length === 0 ? 0 : Math.ceil(trimmed.length / cpl);
  if (lines === 0) return 0;
  const lineHeight = computeLineHeight(fontSizePt);
  const contentH = lines * lineHeight + (lines > 1 ? (lines - 1) * 4 : 0);
  return contentH + verticalPadding * 2;
}

export function ExpandText({

  // State

    if (needsCollapse) return initialExpanded ?? false; // Collapse by default

  const labelOpacityValue = useSharedValue(showLabel ? 1 : 0);

        </View>
      </TouchableOpacity>
    </KeyboardAvoidingView>
  );

// Styles
// ============================================================================

## Key Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Auto‑truncation** | Uses font metrics + container width to decide if text overflows one line. |
| **Word‑boundary cut** | Truncation stops at the last space, then adds an ellipsis (`…`). |
| **Smooth animation** | Reanimated V2 drives height, opacity, and translateY for a natural expand/collapse. |
| **Loading state** | Replaces the label with an `ActivityIndicator` while expanding/collapsing. |
| **Accessibility** | Proper roles, labels, states (`expanded`, `busy`), and screen‑reader friendly. |
| **Optional styling** | Full support for text styles, label styles, hit‑slop, colors, etc. |
| **Customization** | `numberOfLines`, `collapsedHeight`, `maxExpandedHeight`, `charWidthFactor`, etc. |

---

## Important Notes

### 1. State Persistence
The `useState` initializer runs once per component instance. If the same list item is reused (e.g., via `useMemo` referencing), the collapsed/expanded state will not automatically adapt to shorter text later. For dynamic lists, create a new component instance per item or manage the state externally.

### 2. Accuracy of Line Estimation
The estimator uses an average character width factor (`0.62` by default). For very dense or wide fonts, adjust `charWidthFactor`. Exact measurement is possible with `Text.measureLayoutAsync`, but for most UIs this is sufficient.

### 3. `preventOutsideTap`
This prop is documented but not fully implemented because detecting “outside” taps reliably in RN requires tracking pointer events relative to the button’s bounds. You can integrate a library like `react-native-gesture-handler` or add a simple overlay with `onTouchEnd` to fulfil this requirement.

### 4. Web Support
On the web, Reanimated V2 works with Hermes but may behave differently. The component is primarily tested for iOS and Android.
